stem: What percentage of functional CFTR protein is generally required to avoid pancreatic insufficiency?
explanation: Having less than $1\%$ of functional CFTR is generally consistent with pancreatic insufficient cystic fibrosis.
rationale: Even a very tiny amount of function can sometimes prevent the total loss of pancreatic enzymes.

optionExplanations.A: Having less than $1\%$ of functional CFTR is generally consistent with pancreatic insufficient cystic fibrosis.
optionExplanations.B: Approximately $10\%$ function is required for the CFTR protein to work efficiently enough to avoid most symptoms of CF entirely.
optionExplanations.C: This level is typical for carriers (heterozygotes), who generally do not show any symptoms of the disease.
optionExplanations.D: The $5\%$ threshold is generally associated with having the clinical diagnosis of cystic fibrosis but may still allow for some pancreatic function.

source.hint: Even a very tiny amount of function can sometimes prevent the total loss of pancreatic enzymes.
